legend:
Given an array A$$$A$$$ of length N$$$N$$$, whose elements are A1,A2,…,AN$$${A_1}, {A_2}, \ldots, {A_N}$$$, its array of K$$$K$$$-sums blocks is defined as the array of length N−K+1$$$N-K+1$$$ that satisfies Bi=Ai+Ai+1+⋯+Ai+K−1
$$B_i = A_i + A_{i+1} + \cdots + A_{i+K-1}$$

Given an array B$$$B$$$ of length N−K+1$$$N-K+1$$$, count how many arrays A$$$A$$$ of length N$$$N$$$ exist such that their array of K$$$K$$$-sums blocks is B$$$B$$$. Both B$$$B$$$ and the possible arrays A$$$A$$$ consist of non-negative integers. Since the number of arrays A$$$A$$$ can be very large, the answer must be given modulo 998244353$$$998244353$$$.
Note that the sums of the K$$$K$$$-sums blocks array are exact and not modular, meaning the modulo should only be applied to the answer.
input: The first line contains two integers N$$$N$$$ and K$$$K$$$ (1≤K≤N≤2⋅105$$$1 \leq K \leq N \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$).
The second line contains N−K+1$$$N-K+1$$$ integers B1,B2,…,BN−K+1$$${B_1}, {B_2}, \ldots, {B_{N-K+1}}$$$ (0≤Bi≤109$$$0 \leq B_i \leq 10^9$$$), the elements of the array B$$$B$$$.
output: A line with an integer indicating the number (modulo 998244353$$$998244353$$$) of possible arrays A$$$A$$$ formed by non-negative integers such that B$$$B$$$ is their array of K$$$K$$$-sums blocks.
note: In the second example, the only possible array is [2,3,0,8,2,5]$$$[2, 3, 0, 8, 2, 5]$$$.
In the third example, remember that the answer must be given modulo 998244353$$$998244353$$$.
